name: Steam
description: Valve's Steam client, installed silently into a Windows 10 bottle using DXVK. The installer URL always serves the latest SteamSetup.exe, so the pinned sha256 goes stale when Valve publishes a new one: re-download, verify the signature and update the hash. Steam updates itself after the first launch. Two Steam-specific fixes are applied: CoreAudio is disabled for steam.exe only (its microphone format probing crashes CoreAudio inside Wine and kills Steam; games keep audio), and steamwebhelper.exe gets --no-sandbox --in-process-gpu --disable-gpu via AppDefaults\<exe>\AppendCommandLine (without --in-process-gpu the CEF login window paints black). Steam's own UI (steamwebhelper.exe) stays on wined3d: with --in-process-gpu it loads D3D11 in-process and hangs on DXVK, while games use the bottle's DXVK. The Steam in-game overlay (gameoverlayrenderer/gameoverlayrenderer64) is disabled: it hooks the game's main thread and deadlocks it under Wine (frozen game, hidden cursor).
